job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:

Based in the Perth office, you'll provide high-level executive support across multiple time zones. Starting in early December, with a two-week handover period, this initial six-month maternity leave contract offers full-time or part-time flexibility, including five days per week school hours, alongside hybrid working arrangements. 

If you're a polished, proactive Executive Assistant who thrives on keeping senior leaders organised and one step ahead, this could be the perfect next move.

The Role
  • Manage complex diaries, meetings and competing priorities across multiple time zones.
  • Coordinate domestic and international travel and itineraries.
  • Prepare meeting agendas, papers and minutes, and track action items.
  • Provide Board and governance administration support.
  • Coordinate executive workshops, strategy days and leadership events.
  • Prepare correspondence, reports and executive documentation.
  • Liaise with senior stakeholders and manage confidential information.
About You
  • Proven experience supporting senior executives in an Executive Assistant role.
  • Exceptional organisation, prioritisation and diary management skills.
  • Strong written communication, minute-taking and document preparation skills.

Interested to know more? Please apply directly or Call Erin Ablitt 0451 991 529.

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
A&Co Recruitment Partners has partnered with HIF to find their next exceptional Executive Assistant to the CEO.

Love being three steps ahead? This could be your next great move. You’re the person who can turn a chaotic calendar into a perfectly orchestrated day. The one who spots the clash before it happens, knows what the CEO needs before they ask, and quietly makes a hundred moving parts look effortless.

HIF is looking for an exceptional Executive Assistant to partner with their CEO — someone who brings structure, initiative and a little magic to the everyday, and who takes real pride in keeping a busy executive one step ahead.

Based in HIF’s Perth CBD head office, this is a high-trust, high-impact role where no two days look quite the same. You’ll be at the centre of the action, working closely with the CEO, the Board, the executive leadership team and people across the business.

Your world will include:
  • Owning the day: Managing a complex diary and inbox, prioritising competing demands and keeping the CEO focused on what matters most.
  • Being the ultimate prep person: Making sure every meeting is backed by the right papers, research, briefings and preparation.
  • Keeping things moving: Maintaining action lists, following up commitments and making sure nothing important falls through the cracks.
  • Working at Board level: Partnering with the Company Secretary on Board and committee preparation, papers and meeting logistics.
  • Making the logistics look easy: Coordinating executive meetings, travel, events and all the details that keep a leadership team running smoothly.
  • Being the go-to person: Drafting correspondence, managing stakeholder access and helping the CEO present as approachable, professional and well prepared.
  • Improving the way we work: Finding smarter ways to organise information, streamline processes and make the most of digital tools, including AI.
There will also be some practical office and personal support for the CEO. We’re looking for someone who is happy to roll up their sleeves, think on their feet and pitch in where needed.

You’ll bring:
  • Proven experience supporting a CEO or senior executive, ideally in a complex, Board-governed environment.
  • Exceptional diary, inbox and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience coordinating Board or committee meetings, with an eye for detail and a strong sense of confidentiality.
  • Advanced Microsoft 365 skills across Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and SharePoint.
  • Confidence using at least two of Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude in line with workplace policies.
  • A proactive mindset — you anticipate, prioritise and take ownership rather than waiting to be asked.
  • Sound judgement, discretion and the confidence to know what needs attention now, what can wait and what needs to be escalated.
  • A warm, professional and collaborative style, with the resilience to stay calm when the plans change (because they will!).
Experience in private health insurance, financial services or another regulated industry would be highly regarded. Interviews are expected to commence in the next few weeks so please apply today!

If you’re interested in this opportunity, please get in touch with Karen McGlynn on 0406 833 625 or email karen.mcglynn@aandco.au with your updated resume.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
• Lead financial performance
  • Drive continuous improvement
  • Partner with the business
Are you a commercially minded finance leader who combines strong technical expertise with a strategic approach to financial management?
 
Johnson Winter Slattery is seeking an experienced Financial Controller to lead the finance function, strengthen financial governance and provide meaningful commercial insights to support business performance and decision-making.
 
Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this is a key leadership role with responsibility for financial and management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, compliance and the development of a high-performing finance team. You will work closely with senior leadership and stakeholders across the firm, ensuring the finance function delivers accurate, timely and actionable information while continually improving systems, processes and controls.
 
About the role
As Financial Controller, you will provide strategic and operational leadership across the finance function, ensuring financial integrity, effective controls and compliance with all relevant statutory and regulatory obligations.
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Financial leadership and reporting: Oversee the delivery of accurate and timely financial reporting, management accounting and financial analysis to support informed decision-making.
  • Budgeting and forecasting: Lead annual budgets, financial forecasts and performance monitoring, providing insights into financial results, risks and opportunities.
  • Cash flow management: Oversee cash flow, liquidity planning and financial performance against budgets and key performance indicators.
  • Governance and compliance: Ensure compliance with Australian accounting standards, taxation requirements and statutory obligations, including GST, FBT, payroll tax and superannuation.
  • Trust accounting: Oversee trust accounting processes and ensure compliance with applicable legislation, regulations and professional standards.
  • Team leadership: Lead, mentor and develop a multidisciplinary finance team, fostering accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Systems and process improvement: Identify and implement improvements to financial systems, reporting frameworks, internal controls and operational efficiency.
  • Business partnering: Work collaboratively with the COO, senior leaders and operational stakeholders to provide commercial advice, explain financial performance and support business objectives.
  • Audit and stakeholder management: Coordinate external audits and maintain effective relationships with auditors, accountants and other relevant stakeholders.
About you
You are an experienced finance professional with the credibility, judgement and leadership capability to manage a complex finance function and influence outcomes across the business.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • CA/CPA qualified with a degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or a related discipline.
  • 10+ years' experience in senior finance roles, with responsibility for financial management, reporting and compliance.
  • Demonstrated success leading, mentoring and developing finance teams.
  • Strong knowledge of Australian accounting standards, taxation requirements and financial governance.
  • Advanced capabilities in financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting and reporting.
  • Excellent commercial acumen, analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to build trusted relationships and communicate complex financial information to non-financial stakeholders.
  • A proactive approach to process improvement, systems optimisation and strengthening internal controls.
  • Strong ethical standards, integrity, and professionalism.
  • Experience in a legal or professional services environment will be highly regarded.
 
Why join Johnson Winter Slattery?
This is an opportunity to take ownership of a critical business function and make a tangible contribution to the firm's financial performance and long-term objectives.

You will have the opportunity to partner with senior leadership, influence business decisions, lead an established finance team and drive improvements that enhance financial insight, operational efficiency and governance.

If you are a commercially focused finance leader who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on financial management, we would welcome your application.
 
Apply now
If you're interested in this opportunity, apply now including your CV and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience and suitability for the role. For a confidential discussion, contact Phil Scardigno at a&co Recruitment Partners on 0439 074 202 or email phil.scardigno@aandco.au

job.title: Payroll Officer
job.description:
Part-Time | Fixed-Term Maternity Leave Cover | 3 Days per Week

Bring your payroll expertise to a role that makes a difference.
Are you an experienced Payroll Officer who loves getting the details right, takes pride in delivering an exceptional service, and wants your work to contribute to something meaningful?

Lifeline WA is seeking a capable, proactive and people-focused Payroll Officer to join our team on a fixed-term maternity leave contract. This is an opportunity to take ownership of end-to-end payroll in a purpose-driven organisation, supporting the people who help make a difference in the lives of others.

Working three full days per week, you'll play an important role in ensuring our people are paid accurately and on time, while maintaining strong payroll controls, compliance and records. You'll be part of a collaborative team that values trust, respect, connection and excellence.

The opportunity
  • Start date: Ideally 4 January 2027
  • Contract: Fixed-term maternity leave cover through to 30 June 2028
  • Working days: Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday — all three days are essential.
What you'll be doing You'll coordinate accurate, timely and compliant fortnightly payroll for approximately 170 employees, including around 70 full-time staff and 100 Crisis Supporters who are paid based on timesheets.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing the end-to-end fortnightly payroll cycle, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time.
  • Maintaining employee payroll records, including new starters, contract changes, pay point progressions, allowances, deductions, leave and terminations.
  • Applying your knowledge of the SCHADS Award to support accurate pay calculations and compliant payroll outcomes.
  • Administering payroll systems, investigating discrepancies and resolving payroll exceptions.
  • Completing payroll journals, payments, statutory lodgements, reporting and reconciliations.
  • Managing month-end payroll processes and associated balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Maintaining complete payroll documentation, audit trails and strong internal controls.
  • Responding to employee and manager enquiries with professionalism, discretion and a service-focused approach.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • At least three years' experience in end-to-end payroll processing.
  • Strong working knowledge of the SCHADS Award and relevant payroll compliance requirements will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing fortnightly payroll for a diverse workforce, including timesheet-based employees.
  • Experience with ELMO and confidence navigating payroll and HR systems.
  • Practical experience with payroll reconciliations, journals, lodgements, reporting and month-end processes.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies.
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities within tight deadlines.
  • Above all, you'll bring a positive attitude, a proactive mindset and a genuine commitment to being part of a supportive, values-driven team.

Interviews are expected to commence in the next few weeks so please apply today!

If you’re interested in this opportunity, please get in touch with Karen McGlynn on 0406 833 625 or email karen.mcglynn@aandco.au with your updated resume.

job.title: Industrial Relations Specialist
job.description:
Are you an experienced Industrial Relations professional looking for an opportunity to influence strategy, guide leaders through complex workplace matters, and play a key role in shaping positive employee relations outcomes?

We are seeking an experienced Industrial Relations Specialist to join a high-performing People & Culture team supporting a large, complex and highly unionised workforce. Reporting to the Head of People & Culture, this role will be the organisation's subject matter expert across industrial relations, enterprise bargaining, union engagement, compliance, and workplace relations strategy. 

About the Role

This is a hands-on and strategic position where you'll partner closely with leaders and HR professionals to provide expert advice across a broad range of IR and ER matters.
You'll be responsible for fostering constructive workplace relationships, managing industrial risk, supporting enterprise bargaining activities, and ensuring compliance with employment legislation and industrial instruments. 

Key responsibilities include:
  • Providing expert advice on industrial and employee relations matters
  • Leading enterprise bargaining strategy and negotiations
  • Building and maintaining effective relationships with unions and key stakeholders
  • Managing industrial disputes, grievance matters and Fair Work Commission proceedings
  • Advising on enterprise agreement interpretation and application
  • Supporting compliance reviews, audits and industrial relations projects
  • Developing policies, procedures and strategies that strengthen workplace relations outcomes
  • Coaching leaders and HR professionals to build organisational IR capability. 
About You To be successful, you'll bring:
  • Significant experience in Industrial Relations, Employee Relations, HR Business Partnering or a related specialist role
  • Strong knowledge of the Fair Work Act, enterprise agreements and employment legislation
  • Experience working within complex and unionised environments
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise bargaining activities and industrial negotiations
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills
  • Experience managing complex workplace investigations, disputes and case management
  • The ability to navigate sensitive situations with professionalism, sound judgement and credibility. 
What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to lead and influence key industrial relations initiatives
  • Exposure to complex and challenging IR matters
  • Strategic partnership with senior leadership
  • A collaborative People & Culture team environment
  • The chance to make a meaningful impact on organisational culture, workplace relations and people strategy.
If you're a confident IR professional who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with practical problem-solving, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: HR Manager
job.description:
Join one of Australia's leading resources organisations and play a key role in shaping the future of its people and culture strategy.

Based at the world-renowned Greenbushes Lithium Operation, this is an exceptional opportunity for an experienced HR leader to influence organisational performance, build leadership capability, and drive meaningful people outcomes across a complex operational environment.

Reporting to the Human Resources Director, the Human Resources Manager is a critical member of the People & Culture leadership team, responsible for leading the delivery of strategic and operational HR services across the business. Acting as a trusted advisor to executive and senior leaders, you will help shape workforce strategy, strengthen organisational capability, and ensure people practices support both operational excellence and long-term business success.

Leading a team across HR Advisory, Employee Relations, Industrial Relations, and Talent Acquisition, you will foster a collaborative and high-performing People & Culture function that delivers exceptional support to leaders and employees across the organisation.

The Opportunity

This is a rare opportunity to step into a broad leadership role with significant influence across workforce planning, organisational design, employee and industrial relations, leadership development, governance, and organisational change.

You'll partner closely with senior operational leaders to provide practical, commercially focused advice on complex people matters, while also driving strategic initiatives that enhance culture, performance, and employee engagement. The role offers the opportunity to lead through growth and change while contributing to the ongoing success of a world-class operation.

Key Responsibilities
  • Partner with executive and senior leaders to deliver people strategies aligned with business objectives.
  • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team across HR Advisory, Industrial Relations, Employee Relations, and Talent Acquisition.
  • Provide expert guidance on employment legislation, enterprise agreements, policies, and people governance frameworks.
  • Oversee complex employee and industrial relations matters, including investigations, workplace conflict, misconduct, and performance management.
  • Drive workforce planning, organisational design, and leadership capability initiatives.
  • Contribute to enterprise bargaining and stakeholder consultation processes.
  • Coach and support leaders to build confidence and capability in managing people matters.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement across the People & Culture function.
About You

You are a strategic and commercially minded HR leader with the ability to build strong relationships, influence decision-making, and navigate complex workplace environments.

You will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in senior HR leadership or HR Business Partnering roles.
  • Strong employee and industrial relations expertise.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation and workplace relations frameworks.
  • Experience leading complex workplace investigations and managing sensitive people matters.
  • Exceptional stakeholder management, coaching, and influencing skills.
  • A genuine passion for developing leaders, building capability, and creating positive workplace cultures.
Why Talison?
At Talison, people are at the heart of everything we do. This role offers the opportunity to work alongside a collaborative leadership team, contribute to meaningful business outcomes, and help shape the employee experience across a large and dynamic operation.

You'll have the chance to make a lasting impact while leading a high-performing team and influencing the future direction of the organisation.

If you're an experienced HR leader looking for a role where you can genuinely influence strategy, culture, and business performance, we'd love to hear from you.

For more information, please contact Hannah Lelliott at hannah.lelliott@aandco.au.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
• Finance leadership role reporting to the CEO
  • Highly respected provider of Aged Care services
  • Located in Beaconsfield
About us
At InCasa Aged Care & Community Services, we work in partnership with people of all ages and abilities to support them to achieve their goals, remain connected to their communities, and live independently. Guided by our values of respect, compassion and inclusion, we deliver high-quality aged care and community services to individuals of all faiths and backgrounds.
 
With an integrated service model and a strong reputation for excellence, InCasa is committed to improving quality of life and wellbeing for our clients and community members.
 
The Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced and Finance Manager to oversee the organisation's financial health, reporting, and operational finance functions. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role is pivotal in shaping InCasa's financial strategy and supporting our mission-driven service delivery.
 
This hands on financial leadership role is ideal for someone who thrives in a values-based environment, brings strong financial acumen, and leads with integrity, accountability, and care.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Financial Reporting & Compliance - Lead accurate and timely financial reporting, ensuring compliance with Australian statutory and regulatory requirements.
  • Budgeting & Forecasting - Manage annual budgets, financial forecasts and provide strategic insights to guide organisational decision-making.
  • Strategic Planning - Partner with the executive team to influence long-term planning and organisational objectives through robust financial analysis.
  • Team Leadership - Mentor and develop a high-performing finance team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Risk Management - Identify financial risks and implement effective controls and mitigation strategies.
  • Operational Oversight - Oversee daily finance operations including payroll, accounts payable/receivable, bank reconciliations and financial systems.
  • Stakeholder Engagement - Build strong relationships with external auditors, tax advisors, regulatory bodies and internal stakeholders.
About You
Your personal qualities align closely with InCasa's client-centred values.
  • Listen actively and prioritise the needs of individuals and communities we support.
  • Demonstrate empathy, cultural awareness, and respectful communication with people from diverse backgrounds.
  • Act with integrity, diligence, and accountability in all aspects of your work.
  • Collaborate effectively, contribute positively to team goals, and maintain a solution-focused approach.
  • Apply policy knowledge confidently to guide financial operations.
Essential Selection Criteria
  • CA / CPA qualified with tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Finance or related discipline.
  • Aged care sector experience is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated financial management expertise and strong analytical, strategic thinking.
  • Leadership experience with the ability to mentor and build high-performing teams.
  • Proven capability in financial systems, and process improvement.
  • Current National Police Check.
Why Join InCasa?
  • Be part of a purpose-driven organisation creating genuine community impact.
  • Work in a supportive, inclusive and culturally diverse environment.
  • Lead a critical function with visibility across the whole organisation.
  • Enjoy stability, professional respect, and the opportunity to influence meaningful change.
 
Like to know more?
If you are interested in this opportunity, apply now with a short a cover letter and resume. For a confidential discussion, contact Phil Scardigno at a&co Recruitment Partners on 0439 074 202 or email phil.scardigno@aandco.au
